name: Yawiyo
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Hammarström, Harald. 2010. The status of the least documented language families in the world. Language Documentation & Conservation 4: 177-212.
sources.note: Sec. 2.4.19 Walio [ppq,tww,wla,ybx] (p. 192): documentation status of Yawiyo = 'Short wordlist'; 'There are published wordlists in Conrad & Dye 1975 and in Conrad & Lewis 1988, numerals in Lean 1986, and some very minimal notes on grammar in Laycock & Z'Graggen 1975 (752-753) and Laycock 1973 (32-33). Saito 1998 contains ethnographic data on Yabio.' No phonological description exists per this survey.

sources.citation: Saito, Hisafumi. 1998. We are one flesh: Unity and migration of the Yabio. In Yoshida & Toyoda (eds.), Fringe Area of Highlands in Papua New Guinea (Senri Ethnological Studies 47), 93-112. Osaka: National Museum of Ethnology.
sources.note: Nothing; ethnography (villages Lariaso, Arapi; 122 speakers in 1988). Author states his command of Yabio 'remains poor'.
sources.venue: Fringe Area of Highlands in Papua New Guinea (Senri Ethnological Studies 47)

sources.citation: Yoshida, Shuji. 1998. Numeral Classifiers among the May River Iwam. In Yoshida & Toyoda (eds.), Fringe Area of Highlands in Papua New Guinea (Senri Ethnological Studies 47), 113-138. Osaka: National Museum of Ethnology.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: a digital copy exists, behind a library sign-in
sources.note: Nothing. Appendix 'Numeral Classifiers of Yabio' (pp. 132-137) lists 14 classifiers with Yabio example words in a practical orthography; no phonology or transcription notes.
sources.venue: Fringe Area of Highlands in Papua New Guinea (Senri Ethnological Studies 47)

sources.citation: Conrad, Robert J. & Ronald K. Lewis. 1988. Some language and sociolinguistic relationships in the Upper Sepik region of Papua New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 26 (Pacific Linguistics A-76), 243-273. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing. Names three Yabio dialects (Harepi, Yanamo, Woswari), gives cognate percentages, speaker numbers (60-100 at Lariaso), sociolinguistic contact notes and comparative wordlists in 'approximately phonemic' transcription without stress marks.
sources.venue: Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 26 (Pacific Linguistics A-76)

sources.citation: Conrad, Robert J. & T. Wayne Dye. 1975. Some language relationships in the Upper Sepik region of Papua New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 18 (Pacific Linguistics A-40), 1-35. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing on Yabio. Sec. 3.6 'Leonhard Schultze and Frieda Rivers' (pp. 13-14) gives only cognate percentages (Woswari isolect of Yabio 7% with Paupe, 12% with Walio); Table 2 gives a Woswari (Yabio) wordlist with no stress marks. The only stress remark in the paper (p. 11) concerns the Arai languages: 'Contrastive word stress was noted in Ama, and possibly in Rocky Peak, Bo, and Owiniga.'
sources.venue: Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 18 (Pacific Linguistics A-40)

sources.citation: Laycock, D. C. & John Z'Graggen. 1975. The Sepik-Ramu Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study, vol. 1: Papuan Languages and the New Guinea Linguistic Scene (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 731-763. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Sec. 2.11.3.2 'Leonhard Schultze Sub-Phylum-Level Family' (pp. 752-753) gives classification and a noun-classification note illustrated from Pai; nothing on Yabio phonology or stress. The phylum-level list of widespread features (p. 733) includes 'lack of complex suprasegmental systems', but the same passage flags Leonhard Schultze as an aberrant sub-phylum, so this is not a statement about Yawiyo.
sources.venue: New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study

sources.citation: Laycock, D. C. 1973. Sepik Languages: Checklist and Preliminary Classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing. Entry 113 YABIO (p. 33) lists villages (Siabio, Waswori) and says 'Data, including population, from Dye and Townsends (1969)'; no linguistic notes at all for Yabio.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. Newguineaworld: 'Leonhard Schultze River' and 'Central Leonhard Schultze River' pages (newguineaworld.linguistik.uzh.ch).
sources.note: Pages exist in the site tree but are empty (title only, last modified 2024-06-25); no Yabio data or reconstruction posted.
Classification only (Laycock & Z'Graggen 1975; Foley 2018) plus a Conrad & Dye 1975 wordlist excerpt; no phonology.

sources.citation: Foley, William A. 2018. The languages of the Sepik-Ramu basin and environs. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide, 197-432. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
